issues.description: Constructor parameter type for Bookstore differs between the problem statement and the solution repository: the problem explicitly requires init(books: [Book]) but the solution implements init(books: Set<Book>). This mismatch is structural and prevents correct assignment (the solution also assigns a Set<Book> to a property declared as [Book]), which will confuse students and make the intended initializer signature and usage unclear or uncompilable.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the constructor signature consistent with the problem statement and with how books are used elsewhere: change the Bookstore initializer in the solution (and template) to init(books: [Book]) and assign self.books = books. Alternatively, if a Set<Book> is desired, update the problem statement and usage sites to require and use Set<Book> consistently (including changing the books property type to Set<Book>). Prefer the first option to match the stated requirement of an array.

issues.description: The problem statement requires a Bookstore initializer with the signature init(books: [Book]) (an array). The reference implementation in Sources/BookstoreLib/Bookstore.swift instead defines init(books: Set<Book>) (a Set). This creates a mismatch between the specified requirement and the solution API and also conflicts with how Client constructs and passes a [Book] when calling Bookstore(books: books). Students following the problem will expect an initializer that accepts an array, but the solution uses a different collection type, causing confusion and a compile-time/API mismatch.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the Bookstore initializer signature consistent with the problem statement and client usage by changing the initializer in Sources/BookstoreLib/Bookstore.swift to init(books: [Book]) (accept an array). Alternatively, if Sets are preferred, update the problem statement and client code to clearly require and use Set<Book>, but the least disruptive fix is to accept [Book] in the Bookstore initializer.
